text: Compute the bandwidth-delay product for a 1 Gb/s path with a 100 ms round-trip time.
explanation: BDP = 10^9 b/s x 0.1 s = 10^8 bits = 12.5 MB. That is the data that must be in flight to keep the path full, and therefore the receive window a single TCP stream needs. It far exceeds the unscaled 16-bit TCP window of 65,535 bytes, so window scaling is mandatory here.
